text: When designing REST APIs, following best practices is important for building reliable and easy-to-use services. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success, 404 for not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, provide good documentation so developers can understand how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, for example /api/v1/, to manage changes without breaking existing applications. These simple rules help teams create APIs that are consistent, professional, and simple to maintain over time.
